chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Direct-to-disc recording: no chance to sweeten
summary: Herman says the current album could not have been done direct-to-disc, since it needs overdubbing and sweetening; the performance matters more than how it is recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I don't think -- I know we could not have done the things we've done since the direct-to-disc. I know we couldn't have done the current album. direct-to-disc album.
Uh-huh.

At all. There's no way, because you need to sweeten that album, you need to put all the different rhythm sounds and all that in, after you're done. You're proven it's a groovy piece, and that you've done it all. But if you want to compete with the world, and the world is -- "How much time machine can you get going that will upset us," and you better be free to act, don't you think?
Yeah, right.
I do. And --
Well, it's remarkable, anyway, looking at "Road Father," that you could get all that without any kind of a manipulation.
Without -- right, it's remarkable, but what does it prove?
It proves that you prove it a hell of a lot better, too, if you have the other --
Right, I would like to have the time and effort to sweeten and do whatever we have to do.
Uh-huh. Nevertheless, it was a good experience.
It was a great experience, and I guess
it made us aware of the fact that, again, we're called upon to have some kind of confidence in our ability. There's some classical players that have proven that this is a great medium for them.
Uh-huh. Of course, you mentioned a number of times, well, this is what you used to do, anyway, in the 1930's and '40s and --
Of course, but for a much shorter periods.
Much shorter periods, of course, but the process is the same.

And in those years, we were all -- me above all, I was a much younger person and could probably stand a little more pressure, I could possibly stand -- in other words, if the performance was so completely outstanding, but then again, I'm saying the word that tells it all -- performance. Not how it was recorded.
Uh-huh, yeah. The essence.
You really can't go beyond that, can you?
Well, (unintelligible) has these built-in limitations. It's a tradeoff of one set of things --
It's a great idea, and if you didn't do it in your first shot, I don't think you should go back to it.
Yeah. Well, while we're on that, with all
the modern techniques that --
Let me close this door. I'll do it because it's getting --
(Recording interrupted.)
